title: Layer["provide"] is the same compiler-recognized call as Layer.provide and still checks its capability closure
notes: specification/requirements.mdx:80: 'When the compiler knows the complete closure, an unsatisfied capability MUST be a compile error.' A literal element access is the same member access as the dotted spelling: same resolved property symbol, same emitted call. A recognizer that tests only for a PropertyAccessExpression is recognition-by-syntactic-form, and the computed spelling escapes every rule it owns. REVIEW-fable-1.md F4 measured `Clock["context"]()` compiling and PANICKING AT RUNTIME on BOTH backends, which is why only a specification-derived case can hold this closed: the differential oracle is structurally blind to a defect the two implementations share. The body requires `Clock` and `Label`; the layer supplies only `Clock`, so `Label` survives the subtraction. Under the syntactic recognizer the whole `Layer.provide` check was skipped and the program compiled with an unprovided capability — this is a member of the same class as the Context headline, found by enumerating the family rather than fixing the two names the review reported.
